questions.prompt: In static single assignment (SSA) form, each variable name is assigned:
options: exactly once in the program text
questions.why: SSA gives every value a name defined exactly once; phi functions merge values at control-flow joins.

questions.prompt: In SSA, what is a phi function for?
options: Merges a value from whichever predecessor block control came from
Calls a procedure with variable arguments
questions.why: Phi selects a per-edge value at a join. It is the reason SSA keeps one assignment per name.

questions.prompt: In a control-flow graph, block D dominates block N when:
options: D holds more instructions than N
N sits inside a loop nested in D
every path from entry to N passes through D
questions.why: Dominance is on all entry-to-N paths. Dominator trees drive SSA construction and loop analysis.

questions.prompt: Register coalescing aims to:
options: delete all registers in favor of stack slots
split every live range at each basic block
merge move-related live ranges so the copy instruction can be removed
questions.why: Coalescing removes redundant moves by assigning both sides of a copy the same register when legal.

questions.prompt: What does liveness analysis compute?
options: which variables may be read before being overwritten at each program point
questions.why: Live-in and live-out sets: a variable is live where a future read can observe its current value.

papers.caveman: Turning-Stone, First of the Thinking Rocks
papers.real: ACM A.M. Turing Award - Association for Computing Machinery

questions.prompt: Turing's 1936 paper 'On Computable Numbers' answered which question?
options: Can every function be computed by a neural network?
Is there a general mechanical procedure to decide every mathematical statement (Entscheidungsproblem)?
questions.why: Turing showed the decision problem has no general solution by way of the halting problem.

questions.prompt: A universal Turing machine is one that:
options: can simulate any other Turing machine given its description on the tape
questions.why: Universality: one machine reads another machine's encoding. That is the theory under every stored-program computer.

questions.prompt: The Church-Turing thesis states that:
options: quantum machines compute more than Turing machines
any effectively calculable function is computable by a Turing machine
questions.why: It links intuitive calculability to a formal model. It is a thesis, not a theorem.

questions.prompt: The halting problem is:
options: undecidable: no general algorithm decides whether an arbitrary program halts on an arbitrary input
questions.why: Diagonalization kills every general decider. Bounded cases are decidable; the general question is not.

questions.prompt: The A.M. Turing Award is presented by which organization?
questions.why: ACM has presented it since 1966, when Alan Perlis was the first recipient. The prize is $1M, funded by Google.

papers.caveman: Elder of the Stone Ring + Elder of the Spark Circle
papers.real: ACM Fellow + IEEE Fellow - ACM / IEEE

questions.prompt: An h-index of N means:
options: N papers with at least N citations each
questions.why: Hirsch's index: the largest N where N publications each have at least N citations. It rewards both volume and impact.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of double-blind peer review?
options: reduce bias from author and reviewer identities
questions.why: Review decides on the work, not the name. It reduces, never eliminates, bias.

questions.prompt: In computer science culture, top-tier conference proceedings often:
options: serve as archival, peer-reviewed publications equal in weight to journals
questions.why: CS treats conferences like STOC, SOSP, and PLDI as archival venues. Hiring and tenure count them accordingly.

questions.prompt: IEEE Fellow grade is conferred for:
options: unusual distinction and extraordinary qualifications in IEEE fields
questions.why: Fellow is the top member grade, elected by peers for extraordinary accomplishment; the annual class is capped near one in a thousand of the voting membership.

questions.prompt: Reproducibility in research means:
options: independent parties can obtain the same results from the described method, data, and environment
the authors agree with the result
questions.why: The claim must carry enough method, data, and environment for an independent party to redo it.

questions.prompt: The International Mathematical Olympiad format is:
options: two days, 4.5 hours each, 6 problems, 42 points maximum
questions.why: Six problems over two days; each problem is worth 7 points, so the maximum score is 42.

questions.prompt: IMO medals are awarded to roughly the top half of contestants in what ratio?
options: roughly 1:2:3 gold to silver to bronze
gold only, no silver or bronze
questions.why: Roughly half the contestants earn medals, split about 1:2:3, which puts gold near the top 1/12.

questions.prompt: The Putnam Competition is:
questions.why: Two 3-hour sessions, 12 problems, 120 points. Median scores are frequently near zero; it is deliberately brutal.

questions.prompt: A Putnam Fellow is:
questions.why: The MAA names the highest-ranked individual scorers, traditionally five, as Putnam Fellows.

questions.prompt: The first International Mathematical Olympiad was held in:
questions.why: Romania hosted the first IMO in 1959 with seven participating countries.

papers.real: World Champion, International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) - ICPC Foundation
papers.proof: ICPC World Finals results + championship record

questions.prompt: An ICPC team is:
options: 3 students sharing one computer for 5 hours
questions.why: Three students, one computer, five hours, around a dozen problems. Teamwork and machine sharing are part of the test.

questions.prompt: In ICPC scoring, a rejected submission adds:
options: 20 minutes of penalty if the problem is eventually solved
questions.why: Penalty is the time of the accepted run plus 20 minutes per rejected run before it, and only for solved problems.

questions.prompt: ICPC teams are ranked first by problems solved, then by:
questions.why: More solved wins; ties break on lower penalty time. Speed and accuracy are one score.

questions.prompt: The balloon at an ICPC contest:
options: marks a team that is disqualified
signals a problem solved on the scoreboard
questions.why: A runner delivers a colored balloon per solved problem; the floor shows progress at a glance.

questions.prompt: Teams reach the ICPC World Finals by:
options: winning or placing at regional contests
questions.why: Regional contests feed the World Finals. The ladder is the point: you climb or you watch.

papers.caveman: Burden-Bearer of the Two Skies
papers.real: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional (SAP-C02) + Professional Cloud Architect (Google Cloud) - Amazon Web Services / Google Cloud

questions.prompt: A producer must fan out to several consumers, each with independent retries and at-least-once delivery. Best fit?
options: One SQS queue shared by all consumers
A single Lambda function calling all consumers inline
SNS topic fanning out to one SQS queue per consumer
S3 event notifications straight to a database
questions.why: SNS to one queue per consumer gives independent retry, backpressure, and durable buffering per subscriber.

questions.prompt: Archive data, retrieval time up to 12 hours acceptable, lowest storage cost. Which S3 class?
questions.why: Deep Archive is the cheapest class; standard retrieval takes hours, which fits the stated tolerance.

questions.prompt: RDS Multi-AZ deployment is primarily for:
options: high availability via automatic failover to a standby
questions.why: Multi-AZ is failover, not read capacity. Read replicas exist for reads.

questions.prompt: GCP resource hierarchy inheritance flows:
options: organization then folder then project, with policies inherited downward
questions.why: IAM and org policies inherit from organization to folder to project to resource.

questions.prompt: Stateless container behind HTTPS that scales to zero with minimal ops. Best GCP fit?
questions.why: Cloud Run runs containers over HTTP with scale to zero and no cluster to babysit.

questions.prompt: Which object manages rolling updates and rollbacks of stateless pods?
questions.why: A Deployment owns ReplicaSets and drives revisioned rollouts and rollbacks.

questions.prompt: Which command backs up etcd cluster state?
questions.why: etcdctl snapshot save writes a restorable etcd snapshot. YAML dumps are not a state backup.

questions.prompt: Once any NetworkPolicy selects pods in a namespace for ingress, traffic to those pods is:
options: denied except what the policies allow
questions.why: Selection flips the pod to default-deny for that direction. Additive allow rules only.

questions.prompt: Ansible playbooks are idempotent, meaning:
options: applying the same play repeatedly converges to the same state without needless changes
questions.why: Convergence, not repetition. A second run reports ok, not changed.

questions.prompt: Handlers run:
options: only when notified, once, typically at the end of a play
questions.why: Notified handlers run once, in order, at the end of the play unless flushed early.

questions.prompt: Which nmap invocation scans ports and fingerprints service versions?
questions.why: -sV probes services for version banners. -sn skips port scanning; -O fingerprints OS.

questions.prompt: Which command finds SUID-root binaries on Linux for privesc review?
questions.why: SUID files run as their owner. -perm -4000 lists them; stray SUID binaries are classic privesc.

questions.prompt: The OSCP exam pass mark is:
questions.why: 70 of 100 points, with up to 10 bonus points from the lab report. Hands-on, 24-hour exam.

questions.prompt: The CISSP passing score on the 1000-point scale is:

questions.prompt: Bell-LaPadula focuses on confidentiality with which rules?
options: no read up, no write down
no read down, no write up
read and write anywhere with labels
questions.why: No read up, no write down: information cannot flow to a lower clearance. Biba is the integrity mirror.

questions.prompt: OSPF router ID selection order is:
options: highest loopback IP, then highest interface IP
questions.why: Highest loopback wins; without one, highest active interface IP. Explicit router-id beats both.

questions.prompt: STP root bridge election picks:
options: lowest bridge ID: priority first, then MAC
questions.why: Lowest bridge ID wins. Priority is the tunable; MAC breaks ties.

questions.prompt: Which protocol distributes MPLS labels between adjacent routers?
questions.why: Label Distribution Protocol maps FECs to labels. BGP can carry labels too, but LDP is the base mechanism.

questions.prompt: IPv6 hosts use Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) to:
options: resolve addresses and discover routers via Router Advertisements
questions.why: NDP covers address resolution, router discovery, and prefix info. DHCPv6 is separate.

questions.prompt: The CCIE lab exam is best described as:
options: a hands-on, day-long configuration and troubleshooting lab
questions.why: Eight-hour hands-on lab. The written exam is only the gate to it.

questions.prompt: The National Academy of Engineering was founded in:
questions.why: NAS came in 1863, the NAE in 1964, and the NAM in 1970. The NAE is the engineering arm of the National Academies.

questions.prompt: NAE members are elected by:
options: current NAE members, for outstanding contributions to engineering
questions.why: Election by peers is the honor: research, practice, or education that advances the field.

questions.prompt: The NAE administers which major prize often compared to a Nobel for engineering?
questions.why: The Charles Stark Draper Prize for Engineering, awarded by the NAE, carries a $500,000 prize.

questions.prompt: The NAE Grand Challenges for Engineering is:
options: a 2008 NAE list of 14 ambitious engineering goals
questions.why: The 2008 report set 14 goals, from solar energy to reverse-engineering the brain. It is a direction list, not a hymn.

questions.prompt: Election to the NAE is:
options: one of the highest professional honors in engineering
questions.why: Membership recognizes extraordinary contributions and is worn as a credential, not bought.

questions.prompt: The relative minor of C major is:
questions.why: A minor shares the C major key signature. Its tonic is the sixth degree.

questions.prompt: Sonata form is built from:
questions.why: Exposition states themes, development pushes them through keys, recapitulation returns them home.

questions.prompt: First species counterpoint is:
questions.why: Species one is 1:1. Later species add two, three, four against one, then florid.

questions.prompt: A major third spans how many semitones?
questions.why: Major third = 4 semitones. Minor third = 3; perfect fifth = 7.

questions.prompt: When a B-flat clarinet plays a written C, the sounding pitch is:
questions.why: Transposing instruments sound lower than written; the Bb clarinet sounds a major second down.

questions.prompt: In pigment (subtractive) color, the complement of red is:
questions.why: Pigment complement of red is green. In light (additive), red's complement is cyan.

questions.prompt: Hue, value, and saturation describe:
questions.why: Hue is family, value is lightness, saturation is intensity.

questions.prompt: Gesture drawing primarily captures:
questions.why: Gesture is about the action of the whole figure in seconds, not finish.

questions.prompt: Which is a warm color?
questions.why: Warm colors advance: red, orange, yellow. Cool colors recede.

questions.prompt: Leading lines in a composition:
options: guide the viewer's eye toward the focal point
questions.why: Lines, edges, and sightlines steer the eye. Deliberate direction beats decoration.

questions.prompt: Squash and stretch mainly conveys:

questions.prompt: In animation timing, 'on twos' means:

questions.prompt: A walk cycle's four main poses are:

questions.prompt: A storyboard's job is to:

questions.prompt: The 12 principles of animation come from work at:

questions.prompt: Kerning is:
options: space between a specific pair of letters
questions.why: Kerning tunes individual pairs. Tracking adjusts all letters; leading is line spacing.

questions.prompt: A 12-column grid is used to:
options: organize layout and align content across breakpoints
questions.why: The grid gives rules for alignment and responsive span choices.

questions.prompt: WCAG AA minimum contrast ratio for normal body text is:

questions.prompt: Low-fidelity prototypes are best for:

questions.prompt: 'Design thinking' typically starts with:
options: empathizing with the user and defining the problem
questions.why: Empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test. The problem gets defined before solutions appear.

questions.prompt: The Public Service Pulitzer is awarded as:

questions.prompt: The inverted pyramid structure puts:

questions.prompt: In US law, a public figure suing for libel must prove:

options: in the middle of the action

questions.prompt: An unreliable narrator is one who:

questions.prompt: Nobel's will directs the literature prize to:

past and future tense at random
